reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Missing type IIa, which behaves differently under traction.
name: Levine and Edwards Classification of Hangman's Fractures

version.label: Levine and Edwards (1985), types I, II, IIa, III
version.detail: Modification of the Effendi classification of traumatic spondylolisthesis of the axis.

purpose: Classifies traumatic spondylolisthesis of C2 (hangman's fracture).
intendedPopulation: Patients with C2 pars fractures on CT.

options.label: Minimal displacement
options.detail: Fracture through the pars of C2 with displacement under 3 mm and no angulation; C2–3 disc intact.

options.label: Displaced and angulated
options.detail: Displacement over 3 mm with significant angulation; C2–3 disc disrupted.

options.label: Angulated without translation
options.detail: Significant angulation with minimal translation; more horizontal fracture line (flexion-distraction).

options.label: With facet dislocation
options.detail: Type II with bilateral C2–3 facet dislocation.

resultStates.label: Type I: minimal displacement
resultStates.summary: Fracture through the pars of C2 with displacement under 3 mm and no angulation; C2–3 disc intact.

resultStates.label: Type II: displaced and angulated
resultStates.summary: Displacement over 3 mm with significant angulation; C2–3 disc disrupted.

resultStates.label: Type IIa: angulated without translation
resultStates.summary: Significant angulation with minimal translation; more horizontal fracture line (flexion-distraction).

resultStates.label: Type III: with facet dislocation
resultStates.summary: Type II with bilateral C2–3 facet dislocation.

clinicalContext.text: Distinguishes stable (type I) from unstable patterns; type IIa should not be treated with traction.

clinicalInsights.text: Facet dislocation (type III) usually needs open reduction.
Type IIa has a flexion-distraction pattern; traction can widen it.

limitations.text: Displacement and angulation are judged on lateral imaging; thresholds vary between reports.

limitations: Atypical patterns (e.g. fractures through the posterior body) do not fit the types well.

guideSections.what: Four types of hangman's fracture by displacement, angulation and facet dislocation.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess translation, angulation, fracture orientation and the C2–3 facets.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Guides stability assessment with the full clinical picture.

sources.citation: Levine AM, Edwards CC. The management of traumatic spondylolisthesis of the axis. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1985;67(2):217-226.
